messages:
Alex: quick heads-up — ran the fused-paged + autotuned-kernel path on SM86 (cuda 12.1) and saw a sharp perf cliff for long-seq workloads. reproducible locally.
Maria: ugh, cliff as in throughput drop or latency spike?
Alex: throughput. tokens/s drops ~28% for seq=4096, batch=8 compared to same config on SM90. numbers below.
Kevin: can you drop the short perf snippet? and how did Triton vs native CUDA compare?
Alex: short snippet from the microbench (run id: run/2026-03-16-01):
```
config: model=7b, kernel=fused_paged, arch=sm86, cuda=12.1, batch=8, seq=4096
SM86 (fused_paged, triton): tokens/s=62k
SM90 (fused_paged, triton): tokens/s=86k
SM86 (native_cuda): tokens/s=80k
notes: triton fused-paged on sm86 shows ~22-28% lower throughput vs sm90; forcing native_cuda recovers most perf.
```
Sasha: interesting. so triton-generated kernels on sm86 are the culprit? any profiling (s-metrics)?
Alex: did a quick nvprof/metrics: L2 read/write increased, warps stalled on memory, and register spill increased by ~12% in the triton path. stack:
```
- high L2_read_throughput
- increased global loads per output token
- warp_serialize due to load imbalance on paged KV path
```
benchbot: benchmark run complete: https://bench.internal/runs/run-2026-03-16-01 (artifacts + perf counters)
Maria: could be related to memory access pattern differences between SM90 and SM86; SM90 has async-copy improvements and different cache behavior. Triton codegen might be emitting a different load pattern that hits SM86 harder.
Kevin: any interaction with the KV cache warmup or eviction heuristics? paged attention touches KV a lot.
Alex: yes — reproduced a separate test toggling KV prefix cache: when KV cache miss rate > 30% we see the perf cliff amplified. with a fully warmed prefix cache, the delta shrinks to ~8%.
Sasha: so two interacting factors: triton fused-paged kernels produce less favorable memory ops on sm86, and higher KV miss rates amplify the effect.
Alex: exact repro command we used locally:
```
REDWOOD_BENCH_PROFILE=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
./tools/bench.sh --model llama-13b --kernel fused_paged --arch sm86 --cuda 12.1 --batch 8 --seq 4096 --kv-warmth 0.2
```
Maria: any quick mitigation ideas?
Alex: immediate mitigations we tested:
- force native CUDA kernels for fused_paged on SM86 by exporting REDWOOD_FORCE_CUDA=1 (recovers ~14-18% of tokens/s)
- reduce max_batch_tokens (our tessellation heuristic) from 32768 -> 16384 for seq>2048 (reduces memory pressure and evictions)
- tweak KV eviction threshold to prefer keeping longer prefixes pinned during long-seq runs
Kevin: can we add a kernel selection rule: prefer native_cuda for arch<=sm86 when sequence_length > 2048 and kv_miss_rate > 0.2?
Sasha: yes that makes sense. also file a ticket for triton codegen investigation to see why loads are heavier on sm86.
Alex: opened RFC/ticket: PERF-rtl-342 (notes + perf logs attached). proposing changes:
1) quick heuristic change in runtime kernel selector (prod toggle): prefer native_cuda for arch in [sm80, sm86] for seq>=2048 when policy=latency or kv_miss>0.15
2) start per-kernel microbench on SM86 farm in CI to catch regressions
3) longer term: collaborate with Triton team to compare codegen between sm86 and sm90 paths
benchbot: perf alert created: PERF-ALERT-2026-03-16-78 linking run/2026-03-16-01
Maria: for rollout, can we do a canary that flips the selector only for dedicated/qa cluster first?
Alex: yes — plan: canary on dedicated-sm86 pool, monitor token/s and tail latency for 24h, then extend to hosted if stable.
Kevin: i'll add the runtime selector patch and tests. assigning to me and Sasha for follow-up with bench scripts.
Sasha: I'll take the triton repro and start a bisect to find the codegen difference.
Alex: thanks everyone. action items in PERF-rtl-342. ping me if you need the raw nv-nsight captures.
